answers.text:
The bar chart give information about the visits of five age group to the public libraries in one region in 2010 and 2022.

Firstly, in 2010 the group under 15 is the biggest with 4.8 million and the group 60 and over is the smallest with only 2.6 million. The other three group are between 3 and 4 million, so they are similar.

Secondly, in 2022 many group go down. The under 15 fall to 3 million and the group 15-29 fall to 1.4 million, and it is a very big fall. The group 30-44 also fall to 2.6 million people.

Thirdly, two group are different. The group 45-59 rise a little from 3.1 to 3.4 million and the group 60 and over rise from 2.6 to 4.1 million, so now this group visit the library more than all the other group.

I think the young people don't go to the library because they use the internet and the mobile phone for read the books today.

why_this_band.task_response: Figures for all groups are given, but there is no single sentence anywhere stating that the total fell or that there is a young/old split. The final paragraph invents a cause that is not in the data and misreads the figure by saying 2.6 million people, taking the visit count for a headcount.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: There is no linking beyond Firstly / Secondly / Thirdly, and these only serve as paragraph numbers. The sequence is trackable, so the reader does not lose the flow.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: A narrow set of words — big, small, fall, rise, go down — keeps repeating without moving beyond them. There are form errors such as for read the books.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Almost every sentence has an agreement or plural error: the bar chart give, five age group, many group go down, this group visit. All sentences are simple or joined with and.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Drop the prediction in the final paragraph and replace it with an overview sentence stating that the fall only happened under 45; then check plural -s endings one by one.

answers.text:
The bar chart compares how many visits were made to public libraries in one region by five different age groups in the years 2010 and 2022.

Overall, the total number of visits decreased over this period, but not every age group followed the same direction. The younger groups visited the libraries less, while the older groups visited them more.

In 2010, people under 15 made the most visits, 4.8 million, and after them there was the 30-44 group with 3.9 million. The 60 and over group was the last one, with only 2.6 million visits.

In 2022 the situation was not the same. The under 15 group dropped to 3 million, and the 15-29 group had the biggest reduction, from 3.2 million to 1.4 million, which is less than a half. The 30-44 group also went down, to 2.6 million.

On the other hand, the two oldest groups made a growth. The 45-59 group stayed almost the same, with a small rise from 3.1 to 3.4 million, but the 60 and over group increased to 4.1 million and became the group with the most visits in 2022. In total, the visits fell from 17.6 million to 14.5 million.

why_this_band.task_response: The overview states both the overall fall and the opposite direction of the groups, and every group is backed with a figure. The change in the most-visiting group, however, passes as an ordinary detail rather than being reported as a finding.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: 2010 and 2022 are in separate paragraphs, with On the other hand separating the contrasting group; the progression is clear. Transitions are mechanical: paragraphs open with the In 2010 / In 2022 pattern.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: There is enough variety — dropped, reduction, stayed almost the same. Made a growth, was the last one and less than a half do not hold up as collocations.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Relative clauses and comparative structures are used correctly, and most sentences are error-free. The remaining errors (after them there was, the visits fell) do not distort meaning but do draw attention.

answers.what_would_lift_it: State clearly that the ranking changed: under-15s led in 2010, over-60s in 2022. This one sentence would noticeably lift the task response.

answers.text:
The bar chart compares the number of visits made to public libraries in one region by five age groups in 2010 and in 2022.

Overall, library use declined over the twelve-year period, but the fall was confined to visitors under 45; the two oldest groups actually went more often in 2022, and the age group responsible for the largest number of visits changed completely.

In 2010 the youngest readers were by far the heaviest users of libraries, accounting for 4.8 million visits a year, ahead of those aged 30 to 44 with 3.9 million. By 2022, however, visits by the under-15s had dropped to 3.0 million, and the 60-and-over group had moved into first place with 4.1 million, an increase of well over a half.

The steepest decline came among 15- to 29-year-olds, whose visits more than halved, from 3.2 million to a mere 1.4 million, the lowest figure anywhere on the chart. Those aged 30 to 44 also went less frequently, although their loss of 1.3 million was proportionally less severe.

The 45-to-59 group proved the most stable, edging up from 3.1 to 3.4 million. Taken together, annual visits fell from 17.6 million to 14.5 million.

why_this_band.task_response: The overview states three things at once: the overall fall, the fall being confined to under-45s, and the change of hands in first place. The figures chosen support these findings, with no unnecessary reading of individual cells.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: The text is organised by finding rather than by year: first the change in first place, then the sharpest fall, then the stable group. Links are mostly built through reference and time expressions rather than formulaic connectors.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Less common items such as confined to, accounting for, edging up, proportionally less severe are in the right place. The choice of a mere 1.4 million carries the emphasis.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: The past perfect, a relative clause (whose visits more than halved) and contrast structures are controlled. Errors are rare; sentence length varies deliberately.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Use the totals not only in the closing statement but also somewhere that lets the reader feel the scale of the fall earlier (for example, the overall fall as a percentage).
